The core insight is that perception and sensation form a unified process without abrupt transitions. Sensory excitation (E_s) drives neural activity, while cognitive integration (E_c) organizes this into coherent experience. When E_s dominates E_c, fragmentation occurs—this aligns with hallucination as a breakdown of perceptual unity. The perception-illusion continuum implies that illusions are not qualitatively different but rather extreme cases of the same underlying mechanism. In the telescope case, inversion introduces a geometric distortion that reveals hidden oscillatory dynamics in motion, showing how viewpoint affects perception. These primitives map to GSI’s Bayesian inference framework where prior beliefs are updated based on sensory likelihoods, and to GSE’s state-space navigation where attention modulates sensorimotor mappings.
